_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-10-20 05:40:45Z)**_

Line 3 sets which Whisper speech-to-text model the transcriber will load:

```python
WHISPER_MODEL = os.getenv("WHISPER_MODEL", "small")
```

- `os.getenv("WHISPER_MODEL", "small")` reads the `WHISPER_MODEL` environment variable. If it isn't set, it falls back to `"small"`.
- Your repo has a `.env` file, so you can set `WHISPER_MODEL=medium` there (assuming something like `python-dotenv` loads it before this line runs). You won't need to edit the code to switch models.
- Valid names for `whisper.load_model()` are `tiny`, `base`, `small`, `medium`, `large` (plus `.en` variants for the smaller sizes). Larger models are more accurate but slower and need more memory. `small` is about 244M parameters and about 2 GB of VRAM, so it's a reasonable middle ground.

The file only defines the constant so far. It imports `whisper` but never loads the model or transcribes anything. If you're relying on `.env`, call `load_dotenv()` before line 3. Otherwise the variable won't be picked up at import time.
